successCriteria.description: The Employee interface is defined in `src/modules/employee/employee.model.ts` with all canonical fields (id, employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, managerId, department, hireDate, terminationDate, employmentStatus, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt) and imports EmploymentStatus from `src/shared/types`

IEmployeeRepository interface declares all six methods: findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findAll, create, update, softDelete — with exact signatures matching the spec (create accepts Omit<Employee, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt' | 'deletedAt'>, update accepts id + Partial<Employee>, softDelete returns Promise<void>)

EmployeeRepository class implements IEmployeeRepository using the shared db pool from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` and Knex, with all queries using parameterized placeholders (no string interpolation of values)
All read queries (findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findAll) filter out soft-deleted rows with `deleted_at IS NULL`
softDelete sets deleted_at and updated_at to the current timestamp without removing the row; subsequent reads exclude the row
create returns the persisted Employee with server-generated id, createdAt, updatedAt populated; deletedAt is null
update returns null when the employee does not exist or is soft-deleted; returns the updated Employee with updatedAt refreshed when successful
Barrel export at `src/modules/employee/index.ts` re-exports the Employee type, IEmployeeRepository type, and EmployeeRepository class
Jest unit tests at `tests/unit/modules/employee/employee.repository.spec.ts` cover all six repository methods with mocked Knex/pool, verifying parameterized queries and correct row-to-model mapping

constraints: All database access must go through the repository layer — no inline SQL/Knex calls in models, services, or controllers (GP-001)
The employee module must only import from `src/shared/types` and `src/shared/db/connection`; no cross-module imports to other domain modules (employee is a leaf module in the DAG)
No `any` type — use `unknown` with type guards where needed (HARNESS constraint no-any)
All SQL queries must use parameterized placeholders (`?` with value arrays); no string concatenation or template-literal injection of user-supplied values
outOfScope: Employee service layer (IEmployeeService, EmployeeService) — deferred to Phase 8

entityInvariants.invariant: Every Employee has a unique employeeNumber; employmentStatus must be one of the EmploymentStatus enum values; deletedAt is null for active records and non-null for soft-deleted records; managerId is either null (no manager) or references another Employee's id

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when the employee does not exist or is soft-deleted; never throws for missing records
Returns null when no employee matches the given employeeNumber or the matched employee is soft-deleted
Returns null when the employee does not exist or is soft-deleted; returns the existing employee unchanged when the data payload contains no updatable fields

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Employee.employmentStatus must use the EmploymentStatus enum imported from `src/shared/types/index.ts` — the model must not redefine or duplicate the enum

integrationPoints.why: Employee model imports EmploymentStatus enum; all downstream consumers of the employee module depend on this enum being canonical
EmployeeRepository uses the shared pg.Pool instance for all database operations
